findings.evidence: delegation_containment.py `_receipt_chain` picks `first = next(i for i,r in enumerate(ordered_receipts) if r['before'] == start_head)` and drops everything before it. design.md Decision 2 says 'ordered by time such that the first `before` equals the pre-run head'. The comment in the code justifies the skip by recovery, but the artifacts do not describe it. The behaviour is fail-closed in the common case, so this is a documentation gap only.
findings.summary: The classifier skips in-window receipts that come before the first receipt starting at the pre-run head. The design and spec require a chain whose first receipt `before` equals the pre-run head.

findings.evidence: specs/model-routing/spec.md says chain receipts only need an acting worktree outside the delegated one. The code and docs/engineering/model-routing.md also require `remote == 'origin'` and `after == origin_main == remote_main` on every receipt. The code also refuses recovery when a receipt is dated at or before the friction event or names the delegated worktree. The spec lists only 'evidence-bound recovery'. The contract is therefore stricter in code than in the accepted spec, but no behaviour contradicts it.
findings.summary: The normative spec text omits two enforced rules that the design and docs state: the origin-only receipt rule, and the receipt-based refusals in recovery.
